### Summary

The Python bindings are the pybind11 extension through which the same blocks, meshes and options are reachable
from Python. Importing the package first imports torch and the three external packages, sets torch's defaults, and
then loads the extension. The extension exposes the row constants, the restart loader and every component. A
Python driver can therefore run the loop of @sec-ch01-driver with the same calls as the C++ examples.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A, a code map: the initializer, the extension module and the two bindings a driver needs.

**Data.** In: the installed package. Out: the `snapy` module with `kIDN` ... `kICY`, `load_restart`, the bindings.

**Placement.** At `import snapy`.

**Activation.** Import sets float64 and one intra-op and one inter-op thread.

**Guarantee / limits.** A map; `MeshBlock.forward` releases the GIL[^rg-d0276aa97bcd] around the C++ stage.

**Evidence.** `test_python_import_path_python` (exact paths), `test_jit_user_forcing_python`; see the Tests layer.
:::

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path, and the operators are derived
in their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

The initializer {{< code python/__init__.py >}} imports torch, pydisort, pyharp and kintera, imports the extension,
sets the default dtype to float64 and the thread counts to one, and reads the package version. The extension
`PYBIND11_MODULE` ({{< code python/csrc/snapy.cpp PYBIND11_MODULE >}}) exposes the row constants as `kIDN`, `kIV1`,
`kIV2`, `kIV3`, `kIPR` and `kICY`, the representation constants `kPrimitive` and `kConserved`, the function
`load_restart`. It then calls one binding function per component. `bind_mesh`
({{< code python/csrc/pymesh.cpp bind_mesh >}}) binds `MeshBlock.forward` with the GIL released around the C++ call,
so a Python driver reaches the stage and exchange order of @sec-ch01-block-forward unchanged. `bind_layout`
({{< code python/csrc/pylayout.cpp bind_layout >}}) binds `set_process_group`, which the launch helper uses to hand
torch's default process group to the layout. For a stretched $x_1$ (@sec-ch03-globalgrid), `bind_coord`
({{< code python/csrc/pycoord.cpp bind_coord >}}) exposes the option `x1f_interior` and the queries `stretched_x1`,
`x1f_ghosts` and `global_x1f` on `CoordinateOptions`; `bind_recon` ({{< code python/csrc/pyrecon.cpp bind_recon >}})
adds `Reconstruct.set_x1_faces`, which installs per-face $x_1$ rows from a face vector of $n_{c1}+1$ increasing
entries (buffers `interp1.cm_x1`, `interp1.cp_x1`, `interp2.cm_x1`, `interp2.cp_x1`; refused for interpolants other
than `weno5` and `cp5`), and the free builders `weno5_x1_coeffs` and `cp5_x1_coeffs`, which return the rows of a face
vector with no block, `(cm, cp)` of $n_f-5$ rows of 48 and 5 columns; `bind_hydro`
({{< code python/csrc/pyhydro.cpp bind_hydro >}}) gives `balance_column` the argument `stretched=False`
(@sec-ch05-balcol) and exposes the hydro option `conversion_order`, the order of the $x_1$ cell-average to
point conversion of the primitives (@sec-ch04-conv4), whose stub is {{< code python/snapy/hydro.pyi >}}. The stubs are in {{< code python/snapy/reconstruction.pyi >}}. {{< code pyproject.toml >}} declares the build requirements (torch pinned
to one version, kintera, and on Linux commux and pinc) apart from the run-time requirements. It also declares the two
console scripts `pd-combine` and `pd-inspect`. The Python ctests import the package under `SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH` when
that cache path is set ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}; @sec-ch12-build). Import and binding introduce no spatial
order or ghost treatment.

@fig-ch01-python-flow shows the call sequence.

```{python}

#| fig-alt: "Sequence: Python imports; extension bindings; Mesh / MeshBlock API; C++ stage and kernels."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.figures.fig_python_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Why the initializer sets torch's defaults.** Three facts of the code.

1. The default dtype is set to float64 because the solver's buffers are float64
   ({{< code python/__init__.py >}}; {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}).
2. The thread counts are set to one so that a Python driver does not oversubscribe the cores that a `Mesh`
   worker pool uses (@sec-ch01-mesh).
3. `MeshBlock.forward` releases the GIL so that a C++ stage can run while Python waits
   ({{< code python/csrc/pymesh.cpp bind_mesh >}}).

: Implementation anchors for the Python interface. {#tbl-ch01-python-code}

1. Import and set the torch defaults: {{< code python/__init__.py >}}.
2. Load the extension and its constants: `PYBIND11_MODULE` ({{< code python/csrc/snapy.cpp PYBIND11_MODULE >}}).
3. Drive a block or a mesh: `bind_mesh` ({{< code python/csrc/pymesh.cpp bind_mesh >}}); attach a process
   group: `bind_layout` ({{< code python/csrc/pylayout.cpp bind_layout >}}).

**How to use it.** The initializer runs on import; the first lines are these ({{< code python/__init__.py >}}):

```python
import torch
import pydisort
import pyharp
import kintera
from .snapy import *
torch.set_default_dtype(torch.float64)
torch.set_num_threads(1)
torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)
```

A driver then builds options, a block and the loop of @sec-ch01-driver:

```python
import snapy
opts = snapy.MeshBlockOptions.from_yaml("case.yaml")
block = snapy.MeshBlock(opts)
vars, t = block.initialize({"hydro_w": w})
```

A restart goes through `block.initialize_from_restart(path)`, which returns the saved time. Refused: an import without
the three external packages installed (an `ImportError` from the initializer). A restart path is dispatched by
`load_restart` ({{< code src/input/read_restart_file.cpp load_restart >}}): a file that starts with the bundle magic
line is read as a restart bundle. Any other path goes straight to kintera's tensor loader with no suffix check, so a
wrong file fails inside kintera. The row constants a driver indexes `hydro_u` with are `snapy.kIDN`, `kIV1`, `kIV2`,
`kIV3`, `kIPR` and `kICY`.

|---|---|---|---|
| `test_python_import_path_python` | the package is imported from under the cache path and the caller's `PYTHONPATH` entry survives | exact paths; skip 125 when unset | the script's `assert` statements |
| `test_jit_user_forcing_python` | a nested scripted module adds its increment through the Python driver | `assert_close` defaults | library defaults |

: Source assertions for the Python interface. {#tbl-ch01-python-tests}

The assertions are the top-level `assert` statements of {{< code tests/test_python_import_path.py >}} and the
`assert_close` in `main` of {{< code tests/test_jit_user_forcing.py main >}}.

Both tests run on CPU, one process; `test_python_import_path_python` exits 125 when the cache path is unset.
Neither has been run for this report at the pin: **pending a pinned ctest run**. No report check exists for this
section. No ctest calls the stretched-$x_1$ bindings from Python (the C++ tests of @sec-ch03-globalgrid cover the
functions they bind); they were called once at the pin, from the package built from the source tree, and returned
rows of the documented shapes and the four `_x1` buffers.[^py-bind68]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The Python ctests need `SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH` pointing at the package built from the pin; otherwise the
configure step warns that they exercise an installed package, and the import-path check skips with status 125.
The legacy convenience scripts in the `python` directory are not evidence for the current binding signatures.
:::
